subject: Azure private offer: volume cascade & channel commissioning playbook
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Cc: CloudScale Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure private offer: volume cascade & channel commissioning playbook

Team — opening thread to align before we push the private offer to AWS and send the LOI to CloudScale. Key asks from procurement: clear volume tiers, list-price anchoring, and a simple channel commission waterfall they can show their finance team.

High-level constraints:
- Customer wants a 3-tier commit (12m): $250k / $750k / $2.5M ARR equivalents.
- They want marketplace listing eligibility for a bundled SKU and the private-offer discount applied at invoice.
- Channel partner (reseller) expects a 10% starter commission with scaling to 15% at highest tier; finance may push back and ask for pass-through instead of mark-up.

Requests:
1) Ben — can you attach the pricing matrix with list-price buckets + effective net after our suggested channel commission?
2) Laura — confirm if listing the bundle SKU will block private-offer redemption mechanics on Azure marketplace (we've seen oddities there). If yes, we need fallback instructions for the reseller.
3) Irene — any SOC/contractual hurdles for giving the reseller a commission path vs. direct billing? Also flag tax withholdings if commission flows through marketplace.

I propose we present two options to CloudScale: (A) List-price anchor + private offer discount and 10/12.5/15% commission waterfall paid by Redwood as a rebate, or (B) List-price + marketplace passback where reseller invoices CloudScale for their fee and Redwood invoices full list to CloudScale (simpler for us but messy for partner accounting).

I attached a starter pricing matrix and a draft commissioning flow. Plan to sync briefly 10:30 PT unless you prefer async.

— Vivek
VP Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: azure_pricing_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), partner_commission_flow.pdf (document)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: CloudScale Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.com>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer: volume cascade & channel commissioning playbook

On Fri, Jun 1, 2028 at 9:12 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — opening thread to align before we push the private offer to AWS and send the LOI to CloudScale. Key asks from procurement: clear volume tiers, list-price anchoring, and a simple channel commission waterfall they can show their finance team.

Attached updated pricing matrix with an "effective net" tab and two commission models: rebate (Redwood pays partner a quarterly rebate) and pass-through (partner invoices customer). Notes:
- Effective net assumes usage profile similar to CloudScale's PO forecast (70% standard tokens, 30% high-context jobs).
- Commission waterfall modeled as: 10% up to $250k band, 12.5% between $250k-$750k, 15% above $750k. If they insist on 3-band math per your note, we can switch the break points to $250k/$1M/$2.5M.
- I flagged a conservative quantization uplift for the high-tier to ensure we don't underprice the H100 runs.

I'll be on the 10:30 PT sync. If we need to push a second option, I recommend offering a capped commission budget (max rebate $300k) to preserve margin.

— Ben
Director, Cloud GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachment: azure_pricing_matrix.xlsx

From: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudscale.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer: volume cascade & channel commissioning playbook

Hi Vivek / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the matrix. A few clarifying questions from our side: 
1) For option A (Redwood-managed rebate) — can you confirm timing (quarterly vs. monthly) and whether rebate is grossed up for taxes? Our accounting needs clarity for revenue recognition.
2) If we choose marketplace passback (option B) — will the private offer discount still apply at checkout if the reseller is used to procure? We've seen marketplaces block discounts when a reseller adds a margin.
3) On listing: we need the bundle to be discoverable on marketplace for our SOW team. If listing the bundle affects private-offer mechanics, please include a fallback so our SOW isn't delayed.

We prefer a single-invoice flow if possible (Redwood invoices us net of partner commission) but we need comfort on SLA & support routing — if the partner is involved, escalation paths must be explicit.

Thanks — we can take either option but need the final decisioners' recommendation and an example invoice flow before we sign.

— Maya R.
Procurement Manager
CloudScale Inc

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudscale.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure private offer: volume cascade & channel commissioning playbook

Maya — thanks, good questions. Short answers up front: rebate = quarterly payments, Redwood will gross-up only if required by local tax rules (we'll include a tax appendix); private-offer discount will apply at checkout for marketplace purchases if the reseller is registered as our partner and we publish the private-offer entitlement (we've done this for two prior customers, but Azure has edge cases where the bundle listing can override entitlements).

Action plan (mutual action plan attached as a checklist):
- Option A recommended (Redwood-managed rebate) with quarterly settlement. This keeps CloudScale's finance simple and lets us control channel commission accuracy and fraud checks.
- If CloudScale insists on pass-through we will provide a standardized partner invoice template and a short support matrix for escalations.
- Logistics: Laura to confirm listing mechanics & fallback by EOD Monday; Irene to confirm tax/treatment and any contract addendum; Ben to provide capped-commission scenario and final matrix.

We will also prepare a sample invoice and an annotated DocuSign LOI with the two options highlighted. HubSpot deal CS-2028-0421 will be updated after we lock the option.

Proposed next step: Maya, can you confirm preference A vs B by EOD Monday? If yes, we'll send a draft LOI and sample invoice immediately.

Thanks — Vivek
VP Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: partner_commission_flow.pdf; mutual_action_plan_checklist.docx (attachment stub)
